findings.comment: The goroutine body is an unconditional `for {}` loop, so process(task) is invoked repeatedly forever instead of once per task. This contradicts the PR description ("Each task should be processed once") and will spin CPU and re-execute task.Run indefinitely.

findings.comment: The goroutine closure captures the range variable `task` by reference rather than passing it as a parameter. Since the goroutines run concurrently with the loop, they can all observe the same (final) value of `task`, causing tasks to be processed multiple times or skipped. This is a classic Go loop-variable capture bug.
findings.suggestion: Pass the task explicitly: `go func(t Task) { process(t) }(task)`.
